item.title: Re: A train experience based on guilts
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Zyffin. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So my first question was how exactly does the scp / anomaly work. It’s not explained clearly in your Elevator Pitch. How exactly does the train “exploit the guilts of the beings that enter”?

Furthermore, your Central Narrative is lacking in context – you suddenly mention “human experiments” and “future SCPs” but I don’t understand who is doing what. This section should detail a specific story involving your scp: it could be that of a test subject who encounters the scp. It could be from the perspective of a researcher who is conducting the experiments. Regardless, you need to breakdown what actually happens in the story from beginning to end, and the significance of these events. Right now, you’re merely describing the scp in the further detail – this isn’t a narrative.

Regarding your Hook, I’m afraid this section raises more questions than answers because each statement is vague and doesn’t tell me anything new about the actual anomaly.

Lastly, I’m a little worried your language ability at the moment in order to clearly and succinctly explain the concept. There are frequent grammatical errors in tenses and sentence structure that impair the overall clarity of the concept – I’d recommend during a final check before you post stuff in the future or use an online platform like Grammarly to help look for errors.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I may take another look. All the best!

item.title: A train experience based on guilts
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard template, but with an extra "Experiments" section beneath the description

Elevator Pitch: The train is built to replay a situation in which the subject boarding the train has felt most guilty. The subject, upon entering the train car, will cause its doors to automatically shut and no attempts in opening it will be successful. After this, the subject will experience a train ride that accelerates constantly until it arrives at a destination. From the outside, no observations of movement or noise can be noticed. The destination in question depends on the situation in which the subject has felt most guilty, whether it be a rejection, a murder, or failure. This 'nightmare' will cause subjects to become overwhelmed by guilt, nudging subjects to commit suicide or panic.

Central Narrative: The train station in which the SCP is situated was accidentally stumbled upon by Foundation personnel. The station did not seem any less normal than any other abandoned station, but an immense sense of guilt and remorse was felt by personnel upon close contact with the train. Strangely enough, residents of nearby towns have reported that this station did not exist according to their knowledge. Results from experiments include decaying organic materials and animals, disappearances of D-classes, and inhumane deaths of D-classes.

One of the unfortunate D-class requested for the experiment was a caucasian male in his 20s, with a history of murder and arson. Upon the closing of the metallic door, he started to notice the movement of the train. The scratching of the wheels across the rails seems to get louder and louder, and the train movement faster and faster. The train suddenly halted, sending the man flying across the train and knocking him unconscious. He awoke to a dark ally, stretching endlessly in both directions, and the buildings reaching to the limits of the sky. He recognized the apartment beside him as the one that landed him in prison. This is the place where he dies, this is his Hell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Every subject experiences a different kind of 'Hell', and whether they can pass their test purely rests on their own decision-making abilities, one may find that waking up may never happen. In some cases, their bodies will appear in a museum of some sort, displayed as entertainment and education for extraterrestrial beings. How the train was created is also unknown, perhaps the organization has been studying life on Earth for a while now.
